comment: Golden JIT tests. Each case runs 'cmds' over UART; the value of the LAST command is compared to 'expect' (hex). 'known' cases are pre-existing defects.

cases.name: f64_param_cmp
cmds: I64 ff(F64 x) { if (x > 1.0) return 1; return 0; }

cases.name: fn_fib10
cmds: I64 fib(I64 n) { if (n < 2) return n; return fib(n-1) + fib(n-2); }

cases.name: fn_recursion_local
cmds: I64 f(I64 n) { I64 t = n; if (n < 2) return t; return f(n-1) + t; }

cases.name: recursion_local_array
cmds: I64 rf(I64 n) { I64 a[2]; a[0] = n; if (n < 2) return a[0]; return rf(n-1) + a[0]; }

cases.name: loop_do_while
cmds: I64 n = 0; do { n = n + 1; } while (n < 5); n;

cases.name: switch_fallthrough
cmds: I64 v = 1; switch (v) { case 1: v = v + 10; case 2: v = v + 20; break; default: v = 888; } v;

cases.name: struct_recursion
cmds: struct P { I64 x; I64 y; }
I64 g(I64 n) { P p; p.x = n; p.y = n * 2; if (n < 2) return p.x + p.y; return g(n-1) + p.x + p.y; }

cases.name: member_assign
cmds: struct Q { I64 x; I64 y; }
Q qq; qq.x = 5; qq.x = qq.x + 1; qq.x;

cases.name: mutual_recursion
cmds: I64 isEven(I64 n) { if (n == 0) return 1; return isOdd(n-1); }
I64 isOdd(I64 n) { if (n == 0) return 0; return isEven(n-1); }

cases.name: forward_struct
cmds: I64 getfx(F *p) { return p->x; } struct F { I64 x; }; F f; f.x = 9; getfx(&f);

cases.name: f64_struct_member
cmds: struct FVec { F64 x; F64 y; }
FVec fv; fv.x = 1.5; fv.y = 2.5; fv.x + fv.y;

cases.name: f64_struct_ptr_arrow
cmds: struct FBox { F64 w; F64 h; }
FBox fb; FBox *fpb = &fb; fpb->w = 2.5; fpb->h = 1.5; fpb->w * fpb->h;

cases.name: f64_cross_chain
cmds: struct V3 { F64 x; F64 y; F64 z; }
V3 va; V3 vb; va.x=0.0; va.y=1.0; va.z=0.0; vb.x=0.0; vb.y=0.0; vb.z=1.0; va.y*vb.z - va.z*vb.y;

cases.name: f64_struct_param
cmds: F64 getdv(DV *p) { return p->x; } DV dd; dd.x = 2.5; getdv(&dd);

cases.name: f64_lhs_mul_fn_call
cases.note: P4.5 root fix: an F64 LHS multiplied by a function call (defined in an EARLIER unit) must promote as a double, not scvtf the raw bits. The gears bug: 4.0 * half(1.0) == 2.0.

cases.name: f64_struct_arr_member_assign
cases.note: P4.5 root fix: store an F64 function-call expression into a struct array member (g->vertices[k].x = r * MathCos(a)).

cases.name: addr_of_array_elem_write
cases.note: The C JIT REPL returns the *address* (not the value) for a bare top-level array-index rvalue; wrap the read in a function so both engines evaluate it correctly. Compiler.HC handles the bare top-level form too (see scripts/p1-parity.sh).
cmds: I64 abw() { I64 ab[3]; ab[0] = 5; I64 *bp = &ab[2]; *bp = 9; return ab[2]; } abw();

cases.name: global_array
cases.note: Cross-compile globals are the documented one-compile-per-boot limit (J1), so declare and use in a single unit. Bare top-level array-index rvalues also misread in the C JIT REPL, hence the function wrapper.
cmds: I64 g_parr[4]; I64 gparw() { g_parr[0] = 3; g_parr[3] = 9; return g_parr[0] + g_parr[3]; } gparw();

cases.name: auto_decl
cases.note: TempleOS/HolyC 'auto' storage class (behaves as I64).

cases.name: array_init_global
cases.note: Top-level array initializer list.

cases.name: array_init_one_elem
cases.note: 1-element array is still an array (g_has_bracket, not g_count>1).

cases.name: array_init_local
cases.note: Function-local array initializer list.

cases.name: array_init_f64
cases.note: F64 array initializer list stores IEEE-754 bits; 1.5 + 2.5 = 4.0.

cases.name: fnptr_indirect_call
cases.note: Call through a global function pointer (indirect blr).

cases.name: forward_struct_ptr
cases.note: Forward struct used via pointer before its definition (pre-scan).
cmds: I64 gfsp(F2 *p) { return p->x; } struct F2 { I64 x; }; F2 ff2; ff2.x = 9; gfsp(&ff2);

cases.name: include_vfs
cases.note: Compiler.HC #include splices a RedSea file (5 + 2 = 7).

cases.name: array2d_global
cases.note: Global 2D array: row stride must be registered (was a Data Abort).

cases.name: array2d_local
cases.note: Local 2D array: multi-dim declaration must parse (was an internal error).

cases.name: array2d_row_sep
cases.note: Rows must not alias: g[0][3] and g[1][0] are distinct cells.

cases.name: array2d_u16
cases.note: Width-aware 2D element: a U16 store/load must be 2 bytes, not 8.

cases.name: array3d_global
cases.note: 3D array indexing generalizes (per-dimension strides).

cases.name: struct_member_ptr_scale
cases.note: D7: struct-member POINTER indexing must stride by pointee width (U8=1,U16=2,U32=4), not 8.

cases.name: f64_local_array_assign
cases.note: P4.6 root fix: local F64 array element floatness (1.0+1.5+1.5 == 4.0).

cases.name: redecl_float_int_index
cases.note: D14 root fix: a local name redeclared with a different type (F64 then I64) must update its type flags; used as an index it used to compute &b*elem (wild ~18GB read).
cmds: struct RBI { I64 a[4]; }; I64 rbif(RBI *p) { F64 b = 1.5; I64 b = 2; return p->a[b]; } RBI rb; rb.a[2] = 30; rbif(&rb);

cases.name: member_arr_compound_dim
cases.note: D15 root fix: a struct member array dimension may be a constant expression N*M / N+M, like local and global arrays.
cmds: struct CL { I64 m[12]; I64 n; }; struct CC { I64 m[4 * 3]; I64 n; }; CL cl; CC *cc = (CC*)&cl; cc->n = 5; cl.n;

cases.name: decl_comma_init
cases.note: D18: comma-separated initialized declarations (local).

cases.name: decl_comma_global
cases.note: D18 root fix: comma-separated initialized GLOBAL declarations (was a top-level parser gap).

cases.name: fn_prototype_forward
cases.note: D17 root fix: a forward prototype must not shadow the real definition's address.
cmds: I64 fwd_add(I64 a, I64 b); I64 caller() { return fwd_add(19, 23); } I64 fwd_add(I64 a, I64 b) { return a + b; } caller();

cases.name: array_dim_const_expr
cases.note: D29 root fix: array dimensions fold constant expressions (/ and *+).

cases.name: array_dim_shift_sub
cases.note: D29 root fix: array dimensions fold << and -.

cases.name: fnptr_member_dispatch
cases.note: D30 root fix: indirect dispatch through a struct function-pointer member (was shell line truncation).
cmds: struct FDM { I64 v; I64 (*calc)(FDM *item, I64 m); }; I64 FDMmul(FDM *it, I64 m) { if (!it) return 0; return it->v * m; } I64 FDMrun() { FDM x; x.v = 70; x.calc = &FDMmul; FDM *p = &x; return p->calc(p, 3); } FDMrun();

cases.name: f64_ptr_out_param
cases.note: D34 root fix: F64 through a pointer param (`*p = <F64>`) stores D0 in Compiler.HC, X0-bits in the C seed; both must yield 2.5.
cmds: I64 FOPset(F64 *p) { *p = 2.5; return 7; } F64 fop_x = 0.0; FOPset(&fop_x); fop_x;

cases.name: f64_struct_array_member_read
cases.note: D34 root fix: reading struct F64-array members must be float in both engines (1.5 + 2.5 = 4.0).
cmds: struct FSAM { F64 m[2]; }; FSAM fsam_v; fsam_v.m[0] = 1.5; fsam_v.m[1] = 2.5; fsam_v.m[0] + fsam_v.m[1];

cases.name: f0_member_arr_var
cases.note: P7.4 F0: struct-member inline array indexed by a variable (s->arr[var]). Unique names avoid aliasing a module global.
cmds: struct F0AVA { I64 qq1[4]; I64 qq2; }; F0AVA g_f0av; g_f0av.qq1[0]=10; g_f0av.qq1[1]=20; g_f0av.qq1[2]=30; g_f0av.qq1[3]=40; g_f0av.qq2=2; F0AVA *g_f0ap=&g_f0av; g_f0ap->qq1[g_f0ap->qq2];

cases.name: f0_member_ptr_var
cases.note: P7.4 F0: struct-member pointer indexed by a variable must stride by pointee width (U32=4).
cmds: struct F0PV { U32 *zzdata; }; U32 g_f0pvb[4]; F0PV g_f0pv; g_f0pv.zzdata=&g_f0pvb[0]; g_f0pv.zzdata[0]=5; g_f0pv.zzdata[1]=7; g_f0pv.zzdata[2]=9; I64 zzk=2; F0PV *g_f0pp=&g_f0pv; g_f0pp->zzdata[zzk];

cases.name: f0_large_offset_4096
cases.note: P7.4 F0: member offset > 4095 must be materialised, not encoded as an out-of-range immediate.
cmds: struct F0LB4 { I64 ppad[513]; I64 ptag; }; F0LB4 g_f0lb4; g_f0lb4.ptag=77; g_f0lb4.ptag;

cases.name: f0_large_offset_32768
cases.note: P7.4 F0: member offset > 32767 (beyond the scaled 12-bit immediate).
cmds: struct F0LB32 { I64 qpad[4096]; I64 qtag; }; F0LB32 g_f0lb32; g_f0lb32.qtag=99; g_f0lb32.qtag;

cases.name: f0_struct_48_members
cases.note: P7.4 F0: a 48-member struct compiles and the last member is addressable.

cases.name: f0_struct_70_members
cases.note: P7.4 F0: 70 members - exercises the raised (64 -> 128) per-struct member ceiling.

cases.name: f0_many_locals
cases.note: P7.4 F0: 48 locals in one function (raised per-function local ceiling).

cases.name: neg_global_redecl_overflow
cases.note: P7.4 F0: a size-increasing global re-declaration is a HARD ERROR (was a silent reuse of the smaller cell -> heap corruption). Expects rejection (0xFFFF...).
